Rather than just holding, they're asking the board for investment advice and specifically floated the idea of sinking proceeds into local real estate fixer-uppers. Meanwhile, the rest of /biz/ is bleeding out on leveraged plays, so watching this unfold is bittersweet.
clips.text_en_c1: A /biz/ poster claims to have regained access to a dormant 2014 Dogecoin wallet containing roughly 730,000 DOGE, presently valued at approximately 60,000 USD. Rather than simply liquidating the position, the OP is soliciting investment counsel from the board, entertaining the notion of deploying a portion into local real estate fixer-uppers. What makes the thread particularly galling is the disconnect: here is someone who effectively manufactured 60K out of thin air by recovering lost keys, yet still defers to anons for financial guidance. Meanwhile the broader retail crowd watches positions bleed, and the only consolation seems to be the grim irony of it all.
clips.text_en_c2: A poster on /biz/ claims to have regained access to a long-dormant 2014 Dogecoin wallet containing roughly 730,000 DOGE, presently valued at approximately sixty thousand US dollars. Rather than liquidating, the OP entertains the notion that judicious allocation could compound the position into something considerably more substantial. They solicit investment counsel from the board, floating local real estate fixer-uppers as a plausible first deployment. The thread captures a familiar retail fantasy: dormant crypto reanimated, a modest windfall suddenly recast as seed capital, and the subsequent scramble for direction from an audience whose advice, historically, has proven worthless at best and ruinous at worst.

clips.text_en_b2: Back in 2016, the so-called godfather of AI, Geoffrey Hinton, confidently predicted that radiologists would be replaced within five years — ten at the outside. A decade on, the field has done the exact opposite: more radiologists are employed than ever, demand has climbed, and salaries sit comfortably above 2016 levels. The thread is asking who will be the next public figure to embarrass themselves on a global stage, and the OP puts his money on Elon Musk.
clips.text_en_c1: Back in 2016, Geoffrey Hinton, widely regarded as a founding figure in modern AI, confidently forecasted that radiologists would be obsolete within five years and certainly within a decade. Fast forward ten years and the profession has not merely survived but flourished: demand has risen, headcount has expanded, and compensation has climbed well above 2016 levels. The thread invites speculation about which public figure will be hoist by their own hubris on the world stage next, with the OP nominating Elon Musk as a prime candidate for comparable embarrassment. Meanwhile, those pursuing engineering qualifications can take quiet comfort in their continued relevance.
clips.text_en_c2: In 2016 Geoffrey Hinton, widely venerated as the godfather of deep learning, forecast that artificial intelligence would displace radiologists within five years, and certainly within a decade. A decade on, the profession has not merely persisted but expanded: more radiologists are employed, demand has intensified, and compensation has markedly outpaced 2016 levels. The thread's provocation is which luminary will next overstate the obsolescence of skilled labour on a global stage. The OP volunteers Elon Musk as a candidate. For those presently pursuing professional qualifications, the episode offers a salutary reminder that apocalyptic timelines rarely survive contact with empirical reality.

clips.text_zh: 有人問點解人類放棄咗自己原有嘅信仰去信Abrahamic宗教。我都唔知點答，我淨係去六壬堂問sifu lol 🧐
clips.text_en_b1: The OP is asking /pol/ a short historical question: we abandoned our own older religions to worship Abrahamic faiths, so why? The OP calls the people who did this retarded. It is a basic history/migration of religion bait thread with no real answer offered.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread questioning the historical shift to Abrahamic religions
clips.text_en_b2: The OP is asking /pol/ a deceptively simple historical question: why did humanity abandon its older indigenous religions in favour of Abrahamic faiths? He labels the people who carried out that transition as retarded and seemingly expects the board to rationalise centuries of complex cultural, political, and migratory upheaval in a few lines. Predictably, the thread devolves into the usual bait with no coherent answer on offer. Meanwhile, the OP admits he'd rather consult a 六壬堂 sifu for life advice than parse this thread further.
clips.text_en_c1: The OP poses what purports to be a straightforward historical inquiry to /pol/: given that humanity possessed its own indigenous religious traditions, why did entire civilisations elect to abandon polytheistic systems in favour of Abrahamic monotheism? It is, fundamentally, a thread baiting for migration-of-religion discourse without offering any substantive thesis of its own. The OP conspicuously brands those who underwent such conversions with a dismissive slur, betraying more cultural grievance than genuine scholarly curiosity. No coherent argument materialises, and the thread predictably devolves into the usual tribal bickering that characterises such prompts.
clips.text_en_c2: The OP poses a deceptively simple historical question to /pol/: given that humanity possessed its own diverse and ancient religious traditions, what prompted the wholesale adoption of Abrahamic monotheism across successive civilisations? The query is rhetorical more than genuine, laced with contempt for those who, in the OP's phrasing, abandoned indigenous cosmologies wholesale. The thread elicits no substantive answer, functioning as bait rather than inquiry, and the OP candidly admits to having none of their own beyond deferring to a sifu at a local Luk Hang Tong. The exchange illustrates how grand civilisational questions frequently devolve into idle provocation.
